scope.description: Architecture selection for the clinic-erp-back API: choose one primary architecture and bounded secondaries for a security review of request admission, authentication, authorization and tenant separation.
objectives: Name the architecture whose boundary and lifecycle dominate the API security decision
Record bounded secondaries that add a distinct boundary
assumptions: The project builds a NestJS 11 service on Fastify exposing only the six auth routes today
Postgres RLS is the intended tenant-isolation mechanism
limitations: Selection only: no threats, controls, treatments, risks or decisions were produced in this stage; those arrive in the quick analysis.

Prompt bodies for api and multi-tenant-saas were read from the library, but no library registry/revision was read, so identities were matched by filename only and prompt availability is observed within that limited scope.

evidence.statement: Bootstrap registers helmet, compress, an exception filter and CORS from config; it registers no global validation pipe and no trustProxy, and listens on 0.0.0.0.
Global throttler (100/60s), ThrottlerGuard as APP_GUARD, three interceptors, and RequestIdMiddleware on *path.
Six routes, all @Public(), each with a per-route @Throttle of 5-10 per 60s.
No matches: no global or route-level validation pipe is registered, so DTO decorators are inert.
evidence.limitations: Static search only; runtime behaviour not executed.

evidence.statement: AbilityGuard is only provided/exported by authorization.module.ts; it is never registered as APP_GUARD and no route uses @UseGuards or @CheckAbility.
AuthenticationModule registers APP_GUARD GlobalAuthGuard and CommonModules imports it, so the global JWT auth guard is active.
RLS context is applied transaction-locally via set_config(..., true) on the caller's transaction handle using parameterised SQL.
evidence.limitations: The rls-policies.sql that reads these settings was not inspected.

coverage.reason: Primary architecture is api: the dominant boundary and lifecycle are HTTP request admission and per-request authorization in a REST service (EV-001, EV-003, EV-024), not component count. Evidence IDs: EV-001, EV-003, EV-024.

Bounded secondary: the tenant-to-tenant isolation boundary B-006 inside PostgreSQL (EV-020) adds a distinct boundary (tenant identity, RLS context, cross-tenant reads) not covered by request admission alone. Bounded to the tenant separation subsystem; excludes the HTTP admission path already owned by api.
